info.title: Backprod API
info.description:
Every response that is not a success is the §10.4 envelope: one `error` object carrying a stable machine-readable `code`, a human `message`, a `details` object and the `request_id` to quote when asking about it. Driver text, SQL and stack traces never appear in it (§31), in any environment.

**Context is carried in headers, never in the body or the path.** `X-Product` names the product and `X-Tenant` the tenant; a tenant a caller is not a member of is refused rather than silently emptied, and a client-supplied tenant is never trusted as authority — it is checked against membership.

**Money is integer minor units with its currency beside it.** There are no floats: 1999 EUR is nineteen euros ninety-nine, and a rounding rule belongs to whoever formats it.

servers.description: The API is mounted at the root; every path below is absolute.

tags.name: Identity
tags.description: Who the caller is, and what this product and tenant let them do.

tags.name: Products
tags.description: Product discovery, which runs before a product is resolved.

tags.name: Catalogue
tags.description: Plans, features and the offers on sale.

tags.name: Subscription
tags.description: The tenant's subscription, its terms, and what it entitles them to.

tags.name: Billing
tags.description: Invoices, payments, credit notes and the e-invoicing transmissions that follow them.

bearerAuth.description: An RS256 access token from the identity provider, verified locally against its published keys. Swapping provider is an adapter change (ADR-014).

ProductHeader.name: X-Product
ProductHeader.description: Which product this request is about. Required on everything except discovery and the public surface — a resource endpoint without it is refused rather than guessed at (§12.1).

TenantHeader.name: X-Tenant
TenantHeader.description: Which tenant, when the caller belongs to more than one. Checked against membership, never believed on its own.

Error.description: The §10.4 envelope. Every failure has this shape, whatever produced it.

code.description: Stable and machine-readable. Branch on this, never on the message.

message.description: For a person. Wording may change without notice.

details.description: What the code could not say alone — the field at fault, the limit exceeded. Empty rather than absent.

request_id.description: Quote this when reporting a problem; the server log is keyed by it.

Money.description: Integer minor units and the currency. Never a float — a cent lost to binary rounding is a cent an auditor will ask about.

Product.description: `active` is deliberately absent: every product a caller can see is active, so the field would always be true and would only invite clients to branch on it.

ProductConfiguration.description: Free-form product settings. An object even when empty, so a client never has to tell `{}` from `null`.

rank.description: Orders plans against each other. An upgrade is a comparison of two ranks, never of two names (§13).

unit.description: Only a quota has one; the database refuses a unit on a boolean.

OfferGrant.description: What one offer version gives. A quota with no limit is `unlimited`, which is not the same as a limit of zero.

valid_from.description: The window in which this version may be *sold* — not a subscription period, which §12 keeps separate.

version.description: Null only in principle — an offer is presented once a sellable version exists — but typed honestly rather than asserted away.

Subscriber.description: Who is bound. A seat names the person; a tenant subscription does not.

SubscriptionTerms.description: Snapshotted when the subscription was taken out, not read from the offer now — which is the whole point of snapshotting them (§13.1). Changing an offer never rewrites what somebody already agreed to.

term_months.description: How long the contract runs. Null means no fixed term.

commitment_months.description: How much of the term the customer cannot leave. Never longer than the term; the database refuses it.

early_termination.description: What leaving before the commitment ends costs.

notice_days.description: How long before the term ends the prior notice is due. Zero means none is configured, and none is sent.

current_period_start.description: The *subscription's* period, which §12 keeps distinct from the offer's commercial window.

current_period_end.description: Null for a CUSTOM billing period, which has no end to be past.

CancellationDecision.description: Why the answer is what it is. What a customer needs is not `cancelled: true` but *when* it takes effect and which rule decided that (§13.1) — so the rule's id travels with the decision and the reasons are in plain words.

rule_id.description: Which rule decided. Stable, and the thing to quote in a support conversation.

chargeable_months.description: Months of the commitment still owed. Counted from the end of the period already paid for, not from today.

SubscriptionEvent.description: The history (§18). Every transition writes one, including those nobody performed — an expiry has no actor because the clock did it.

actor_user_id.description: Null when the clock did it rather than a person.

limit.description: Null means two different things, so `unlimited` says which.

source.description: What produced it — a subscription grant, or an override negotiated outside one.

BillingMoney.description: Integer minor units and the currency. Note the field is `minor_units` here, while the catalogue uses `amount_minor_units` for the same idea — an inconsistency the contract records rather than hides.

PartySnapshot.description: Supplier or customer **as they were when the document was issued**, copied rather than referenced (§25). A later change of address must not rewrite an invoice already sent, and an RGPD erasure deliberately leaves this standing.

vat_rate_basis_points.description: Basis points, as stored. Sending "20%" would lose 5.5% to whatever the client's parser did with the half.

source_offer_version_id.description: Which offer version priced this line. Attribution runs through here, never through the subscription's *current* offer, which would credit today's offer with money an older one earned.

number.description: Null until issued. A draft has no legal number, and inventing a placeholder is how a gap enters a sequence that must not have one.

final.description: Whether it can still change. A final invoice is corrected by a credit note, never edited.

taxes.description: One row per jurisdiction and rate. They sum to the invoice's VAT — a test asserts it.

CreditNote.description: How a final invoice is corrected. Its own gapless sequence, separate from the invoices'.

direction.description: Always CREDIT. Present so a client reading a mixed ledger never has to infer the sign.

provider.description: Which PSP. The domain never names one; this is the adapter that was used.

final.description: Whether the status can still move. A webhook arriving after this is ignored rather than applied twice.

method.description: How it was paid. Never card data — §24 forbids storing that here at all.

failure_reason.description: The provider's category, never its raw message: that can carry an endpoint or a token, and this field is served over the API (§31).

Transmission.description: An invoice's journey to a certified e-invoicing platform (§25.1). Four states, and a rejection is a settled outcome rather than an error to retry blindly.

BillingProfile.description: Who the tenant is, for invoicing. Copied onto each document at issue — changing it never rewrites an invoice already sent.

Refund.description: A refund against a settled payment.

Unauthenticated.description: No credential, or one that did not verify.

PermissionDenied.description: Authenticated, but not allowed to do this here.

NotFound.description: No such thing — or none this caller may see. The two are deliberately indistinguishable.

TooManyRequests.description: The caller has spent its allowance for the current window (§31).

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait. A client told only "too many" would guess, and a guessing client retries too soon.

InternalError.description: A controlled 500 (§37.9). The diagnostic detail is in the server log against this request_id, never on the wire.

get.description: The one path reachable with no credential at all. It answers from the process alone: an unreachable database must not make the process look dead to an orchestrator, so this stays up when data is down.

get.summary: The caller, as this product and tenant see them
get.description: Everything the §10.6 chain resolved: who, where, and what that combination permits. `roles` and `permissions` are the tenant's grant; `capabilities` are what the subscription bought. Authorisation asks about capabilities, never about a plan's name (§13).

capabilities.description: Feature codes the tenant is entitled to here.

patch.description: Partial by design: an absent `display_name` leaves it untouched, an explicit `null` clears it. Those are different requests and are not collapsed into one.

422.description: The body was well-formed JSON but not acceptable — a display name past its length, say.

display_name.description: Absent leaves it alone; null clears it.

get.summary: The caller's roles and permissions here
get.description: The authorisation half of `/me`, on its own, for a client that wants to refresh what is allowed without re-reading the profile.

200.description: Roles and permissions for this product and tenant.

get.description: Capability codes, resolved once by the context chain from what is in force now. A lapsed subscription grants nothing without anything having to sweep it first — entitlement asks the clock.

Runs before a product is resolved, and must: a client cannot send `X-Product` until it knows which products it may use, so requiring one here would make discovery depend on its own result. Authorisation is per product, from membership.

200.description: The products available to this caller.

get.description: Named in the path rather than the header, because this is discovery: the caller is asking about a product, not acting inside one.

get.summary: A product's features and configuration together
get.description: One round trip for what a client needs to render a product before choosing it.
The catalogue of features a product defines, independent of what any tenant has bought.
An object even when empty, so a client never has to tell `{}` from `null`.
Ordered by `rank`, which is what an upgrade compares. Nothing in the platform branches on a plan's *name* (§13, and a CI gate says so).
The vocabulary entitlements are expressed in. A quota carries its unit; a boolean must not.
Only what may be sold *now*: an offer whose version's validity window has closed is absent rather than marked expired, because a client that can see it will eventually try to buy it.
The offer with its plan and the version that prices it, including every grant that version carries.

get.summary: The current subscription, its history and its events
get.description: Three answers in one: what is in force now, everything that came before, and the transitions between them. `subscription` is null when the tenant has never subscribed — not the same as a cancelled one, and history tells them apart.

post.description: `seat: true` subscribes the caller personally rather than the tenant. A tenant may hold one active subscription and a person one active seat — both are unique indexes, so two simultaneous requests cannot produce two.

seat.description: Subscribe the caller personally instead of the tenant.

409.description: Already subscribed, or the offer is not on sale.

post.description: The subscription keeps its identity and its history; only what it grants changes. An upgrade compares the plans' ranks, never their names (§13).

200.description: The subscription on its new offer.

409.description: No subscription to change, or the offer is not on sale.

post.summary: Cancel, or say why it cannot be cancelled
post.description: Returns the subscription **and the decision**. A refusal is a 200 with `accepted: false` and the rule that refused it, not an error: the request was understood and answered, and the customer needs to know which term binds them. Where leaving early costs money, the buy-out invoice is raised in the same transaction and named here.

immediately.description: Ask to end now rather than at the next boundary. The policy still decides; asking does not make it so.

seat.description: Cancel the caller's own seat rather than the tenant's subscription.

200.description: The subscription and what cancelling did, or would do.

charge_invoice_id.description: The early-termination invoice, when one was raised. Null when leaving cost nothing.

get.description: The same decision the cancel endpoint would return, without performing it — so a client can show the consequence before the customer commits to it.

parameters.name: seat
parameters.description: Present asks about the caller's own seat rather than the tenant's subscription, matching the cancel endpoint it predicts.

200.description: The subscription and the hypothetical decision.

post.description: Only before it takes effect. Resuming clears the effective date as well as the flag — a subscription claiming to end on a date it no longer honours is refused by the database.

get.summary: What the tenant is entitled to
get.description: Resolved from what is in force now, so a lapsed subscription grants nothing without anything having had to sweep it first. This is the *tenant's* view: a seat held by one colleague still appears here, which is a known gap rather than a design.
Every field is nullable: a tenant that has not filled this in yet gets nulls rather than a 404, because the profile is a property of the tenant and always exists conceptually.

put.description: PUT, not PATCH: this is the whole identity, and a partial update of a legal address is how half an address reaches an invoice. Only `legal_name` is required.

422.description: A field was present but unacceptable — a country code that is not two letters, say.

get.description: Newest first, paginated.

post.summary: Raise the invoice for the current subscription
post.description: Takes no body: what to bill is the subscription in force, and letting a client name the amount would let a client name the amount. Issuing assigns the next number in a gapless sequence, under a lock — two simultaneous requests cannot both take it.

409.description: Nothing to invoice, or the period is already invoiced.

get.description: With its lines and its tax rows. The party snapshots are as of issue, not as the tenant is now.

post.description: For payment received outside the platform — a transfer, a cheque. Money taken through a PSP arrives by webhook instead and must not be recorded here as well.

409.description: Not in a state that can be paid — a draft, or already paid.

post.description: Only while it is still a draft. A final invoice is corrected by a credit note, never cancelled — cancelling one that has been sent would leave a hole in the legal sequence.

409.description: Already final; issue a credit note instead.

post.summary: Begin a payment through the provider
post.description: Returns the payment **and the provider's client secret**, which is what the browser needs to complete the charge. Card data never reaches this API (§24): the client talks to the provider directly and the platform learns the outcome by webhook.

201.description: The pending payment and its client secret.

client_secret.description: Hand to the provider's client SDK. Never logged, never stored.

409.description: The invoice cannot be paid — a draft, cancelled, or already settled.

post.description: The only way to change a document that has been issued. The credit note takes the next number in its **own** gapless sequence.

409.description: The invoice is not in a state that can be credited.

post.summary: Send an invoice to the e-invoicing platform
post.description: 202, not 200: submission is handed to the provider and settles later. Poll the transmissions below, or wait for the webhook. **Today this reaches a stub** — no certified platform is connected yet (R3).

409.description: The invoice is not issued, or has already been transmitted.

get.description: Every attempt, not just the last: a rejection followed by an acceptance is two facts, and the first is the one an auditor asks about.
Newest first, paginated.
Including why it failed, as a code and a category — never the provider's raw message, which can carry an endpoint or a token (§31).

post.description: 202: the provider decides when the money moves. Omitting `amount_minor_units` refunds the whole payment; a partial refund may not exceed what is left unrefunded, and the database enforces that rather than the caller remembering it.

reason.description: Why. Upper-cased and stored as a category.

202.description: The refund, accepted by the provider.

409.description: Not refundable — unsettled, or already fully refunded.

get.description: Newest first, paginated.
